answers.reasoning: Each tristimulus component integrates the received spectrum weighted by one cone sensitivity; it is not a wavelength, pixel coordinate or illumination-invariant material constant.
The shown front-end order is optics, sensor, ISO gain, ADC.
The actual ISP arrows order demosaic, denoise, white balance, gamma, compression; this is a source-specific simplified sequence.
Silicon photosites convert light into electrical signals; they do not store semantic labels or replace electronics with lenses.
CCD shifts charge to shared conversion/output circuitry; the CMOS drawing shows local conversion with addressed readout.
Both sensor types transduce incident light into an electrical image signal; readout architecture is the distinction.
The inaccurate CMOS expansion is separable from the readout mechanism and should remain recorded as a source issue.
One Bayer tile contains two green, one red and one blue filter site.
Four RGB triplets require12 scalars; four were measured, leaving8 estimates.
ISO gain amplifies an existing electrical signal; fixed illumination/time does not acquire more photons merely by gain.
floor(8*.6)=floor4.8=4, already within0..7. The supplied quantizer defines the convention.
Demosaicing estimates the two missing color-channel values at each CFA site from neighbors.
Shot noise involves photon-count variation; dark current involves thermally generated electrons.
Denoising directly targets graininess; sharpening alone can enhance noise rather than remove it.
Edge enhancement is not a guarantee of recovering information lost in capture.
Reciprocal gains1/.5=2,1/.4=2.5,1/.25=4 produce equal unit channels.
White-balance channel gains do not generally correct spectral cross-channel differences; color correction can mix channels.
Identical matrix dimensions do not imply identical domains: augmented color vectors differ from homogeneous spatial points. The fourth color coordinate is not inferred from the source.
sqrt(.25)=.5 illustrates the explicitly supplied nonlinear gamma-like encoding, not JPEG or white balance.
Gamma changes intensity representation; final compression changes storage/transmission representation.
The drawing places the physical sensor behind optics and a virtual image plane in front.
The normal indicates local surface orientation; it is distinct from the reflected camera-bound ray and image axes.
Rays from the object top cross the aperture to the lower rear image plane, causing inversion.
A small aperture admits little light; a lens collects a larger bundle and focuses it.
As1/d_o approaches0,1/d_i approaches1/f and d_i approachesf.
Signed magnification=-d_i/d_o=-1/3, so a30mm object gives-10mm.
The positive absolute-distance equation is scoped to the illustrated real configuration; virtual images need an explicit consistent sign convention.
The front virtual plane gives positive x=fX/Z and y=fY/Z under the stated camera coordinates.
A common positive scale cancels in X/Z and Y/Z; changing only f, depth or transverse coordinates does not.
